rationale:
Decision: split into three independent children. The selected node's own proof is then a 4-line assembly.

The supplied 9-step proof combines three kinds of mathematics with disjoint hypotheses. Each is a genuine, reusable obligation:
- approx_tangent_le_flat (dgcr_atg_approxTangent_le_of_flat) is supplied steps 2–8, abstracted: the graph Σ, the plane L = range DΦ(v₀) and the differentiability estimate become an arbitrary set S, an arbitrary subspace T and a flatness hypothesis. It states: if Hⁿ((A ∩ B_r(x)) ∖ S) = 0 and S is flat at x along T, then every approximate tangent plane Q of A at x satisfies Q ≤ T. This is a pure Hausdorff-measure blow-up fact about Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (test function, Lipschitz images of null sets, uniqueness of limits, spt Hⁿ⌞Q = Q). It uses no graph and no derivative.
- graph_image_flat (dgcr_atg_graph_image_flat) is supplied step 1 (coercivity), step 4 and the case 'a ∈ Σ' of step 5. It states: if u is differentiable at v₀, then Φ(D) is flat at Φ(v₀) along range DΦ(v₀) for any set D. This is differential calculus only.
- graph_tangent_finrank (dgcr_atg_graph_tangent_finrank) is supplied step 1. DΦ(v₀) = ι + ι'∘Du(v₀) is injective by orthogonality, so finrank range DΦ(v₀) = n. This is linear algebra only.
The three children are mutually independent (depends_on = []). Each child's natural proof is the corresponding supplied steps, specialized; no new mathematics is introduced.

How the children imply the selected statement (supplied steps 2 and 9). This compiles.
(a) u is C¹ on the open ball B_s(0), which contains v₀, so u is differentiable at v₀: (hu.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (isOpen_ball.mem_nhds hv₀).
(b) graph_image_flat with D := ball 0 s is literally the flatness hypothesis of approx_tangent_le_flat for S := Φ '' ball 0 s, x := z + ι v₀ + ι' (u v₀) and T := L.
(c) approx_tangent_le_flat with P := n + k, the given A, r, Q, the hypothesis 0 < r, the null hypothesis and hQ gives Q ≤ L.
(d) hQ.finrank_eq gives finrank Q = n, and graph_tangent_finrank gives finrank L = n. So Q = L by Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes lie in any direction along which the set is almost everywhere flat
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S, A ⊆ ℝ^P (ℝ^P = Euclid P), x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0, and let Q, T be linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Suppose Hⁿ((A ∩ B_r(x)) ∖ S) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] and B_r(x) is the open ball. Suppose also that S is flat at x along T: for every ε > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that every y ∈ S with dist(y, x) < ρ admits some t ∈ T with ‖y − x − t‖ ≤ ε‖y − x‖. If A has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4), then Q ⊆ T. Here HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ → 0⁺, with η_{x,λ}(a) = λ⁻¹(a − x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (Q T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < r → μHE[n] ((A ∩ ball x r) \ S) = 0 → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ y ∈ S, dist y x < ρ → ∃ t ∈ T, ‖y - x - t‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - x‖) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → Q ≤ T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–8 of the parent-supplied proof of dgcr_approxTangent_eq_graph_tangent, generalized as follows:
- the graph Σ becomes an arbitrary set S;
- the plane L = range DΦ(v₀) becomes an arbitrary subspace T;
- the coercivity and differentiability estimates of supplied steps 1 and 4, as used in step 5, become the flatness hypothesis.
The quantity the supplied proof calls ε (namely infDist(y, L)) is called δ here, because ε now denotes the flatness parameter.

Notation:
- ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hⁿ = μHE[n].
- For λ ∈ ℝ, η_λ(a) := blowUpMap x λ a = λ⁻¹(a − x) (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap).
- N := (A ∩ B_r(x)) ∖ S, so Hⁿ(N) = 0 by hypothesis.
- HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_λ(A)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ → 0⁺. Each integral is against Hⁿ restricted to the indicated set.

Formalization note: unless split further, this is a machine leaf: one theorem appended to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, with no new import or helper. Every lemma cited below is in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.

1. T is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and it is nonempty since 0 ∈ T. Let y ∈ Q; we show y ∈ T. Suppose, for contradiction, that y ∉ T.

2. Then δ := infDist(y, T) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). Put R := ‖y‖ + δ > 0 and ε := δ/(4R) > 0.

3. Let g(w) := max(0, δ/2 − dist(w, y)).
- g is continuous and g ≥ 0.
- g(w) = 0 whenever w ∉ B̄_{δ/2}(y), since then δ/2 − dist(w, y) < 0.
- g(w) > 0 whenever w ∈ B_{δ/2}(y).
Closed balls of ℝ^P are compact, so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro). Hence g defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) with f(w) = g(w) for all w.

4. Apply the flatness hypothesis with this ε. It gives ρ > 0 such that every a ∈ S with dist(a, x) < ρ admits t ∈ T with ‖a − x − t‖ ≤ ε‖a − x‖. Put λ₀ := min(ρ, r)/R > 0.

5. Claim: for every λ with 0 < λ < λ₀, η_λ(A) ∩ B̄_{δ/2}(y) ⊆ η_λ(N).
Let a ∈ A with w := η_λ(a) ∈ B̄_{δ/2}(y).
- Bounds. a − x = λw, and ‖w‖ ≤ ‖y‖ + dist(w, y) ≤ ‖y‖ + δ/2 < R. Hence ‖a − x‖ = λ‖w‖ < λR < min(ρ, r), the last step because λ < λ₀. In particular a ∈ B_r(x).
- Suppose a ∈ S. Since dist(a, x) = ‖a − x‖ < ρ, step 4 gives t ∈ T with ‖a − x − t‖ ≤ ε‖a − x‖.
- Then λ⁻¹t ∈ T and w − λ⁻¹t = λ⁻¹(a − x − t). Therefore dist(w, λ⁻¹t) = λ⁻¹‖a − x − t‖ ≤ λ⁻¹ε‖a − x‖ = ε‖w‖ < εR = δ/4.
- So infDist(w, T) ≤ dist(w, λ⁻¹t) < δ/4 (Metric.infDist_le_dist_of_mem).
- But infDist(y, T) ≤ infDist(w, T) + dist(y, w) (Metric.infDist_le_infDist_add_dist), and dist(y, w) ≤ δ/2. Together these give infDist(w, T) ≥ δ − δ/2 = δ/2, a contradiction.
Hence a ∉ S. So a ∈ (A ∩ B_r(x)) ∖ S = N, and w = η_λ(a) ∈ η_λ(N).

6. Fix λ > 0. The map η_λ is λ⁻¹-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, since ‖η_λ(a) − η_λ(b)‖ = λ⁻¹‖a − b‖. Hence Hⁿ(η_λ(N)) ≤ (λ⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(N) = 0 (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, with constant Real.toNNReal λ⁻¹). By step 5 and monotonicity, Hⁿ(η_λ(A) ∩ B̄_{δ/2}(y)) = 0 for every λ ∈ (0, λ₀).

7. Fix λ ∈ (0, λ₀).
- The closed ball is measurable, so (Hⁿ⌞η_λ(A))(B̄_{δ/2}(y)) = Hⁿ(B̄_{δ/2}(y) ∩ η_λ(A)) = 0 by step 6 (Measure.restrict_apply). Measurability of η_λ(A) is not needed.
- Hence Hⁿ⌞η_λ(A)-almost every w lies outside B̄_{δ/2}(y) (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), and there f(w) = 0 by step 3.
- So f = 0 almost everywhere for Hⁿ⌞η_λ(A), and ∫_{η_λ(A)} f dHⁿ = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).

8. The interval (0, λ₀) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT).
- By step 7, the function λ ↦ ∫_{η_λ(A)} f dHⁿ is eventually equal to the constant 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, so it tends to 0 (Tendsto.congr' with tendsto_const_nhds).
- By the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q applied to f, the same function tends to ∫_Q f dHⁿ.
- Since 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter, uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique) gives ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.

9. On the other hand, finrank Q = n. Hence:
- μ_Q := Hⁿ⌞Q is a regular measure, in particular finite on compact sets (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule);
- its support is Q (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule).
f is continuous with compact support, so it is μ_Q-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), and f ≥ 0. The support of f contains the open ball B_{δ/2}(y), which is a neighbourhood of y. As y ∈ Q = supp μ_Q, μ_Q(support f) ≥ μ_Q(B_{δ/2}(y)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall). Hence ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). This contradicts step 8.

10. Therefore y ∈ T. As y ∈ Q was arbitrary, Q ≤ T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Assume y ∈ Q ∖ T. Since T is closed, δ := infDist(y, T) > 0. Put R := ‖y‖ + δ and ε := δ/(4R), and test with f := max(0, δ/2 − dist(·, y)) ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
Flatness at ε gives ρ. For 0 < λ < min(ρ, r)/R, η_λ(A) ∩ B̄_{δ/2}(y) ⊆ η_λ((A ∩ B_r(x)) ∖ S): a point a ∈ S would put η_λ(a) within δ/4 of T, whereas infDist(·, T) ≥ δ/2 on B̄_{δ/2}(y).
η_λ is λ⁻¹-Lipschitz, so that image is Hⁿ-null. Since f vanishes off B̄_{δ/2}(y), ∫_{η_λ(A)} f dHⁿ = 0 for all λ ∈ (0, min(ρ, r)/R).
The approximate-tangent limit along 𝓝[>] 0 and uniqueness of limits give ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.
Hⁿ⌞Q is locally finite with support Q ∋ y, and f > 0 on B_{δ/2}(y), so ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0. This contradiction shows Q ≤ T.

subproblems.title: The image of an orthogonal graph map is flat along its tangent plane
subproblems.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, and let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v ∈ ℝⁿ, w ∈ ℝ^k. Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, D ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set, and v₀ ∈ ℝⁿ with u differentiable at v₀. Put Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v). Then for every ε > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that every y ∈ Φ(D) with dist(y, Φ(v₀)) < ρ admits some t ∈ range DΦ(v₀) with ‖y − Φ(v₀) − t‖ ≤ ε‖y − Φ(v₀)‖. Here DΦ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ Φ v₀, viewed as a linear map.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (u : Euclid n → Euclid k) (z : Euclid (n + k)) (D : Set (Euclid n)) (v₀ : Euclid n), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → DifferentiableAt ℝ u v₀ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∀ y ∈ (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) '' D, dist y (z + ι v₀ + ι' (u v₀)) < ρ → ∃ t ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) v₀ : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)), ‖y - (z + ι v₀ + ι' (u v₀)) - t‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - (z + ι v₀ + ι' (u v₀))‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: three pieces of the parent-supplied proof of dgcr_approxTangent_eq_graph_tangent:
- step 1: coercivity ‖v − v′‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v′)‖, and differentiability of Φ at v₀;
- step 4: the differentiability estimate;
- the case 'a ∈ Σ' of step 5.
The parent's domain D = B_s(0) is replaced by an arbitrary set D ⊆ ℝⁿ; only differentiability of u at v₀ is used.

Notation: ℝ^m = Euclid m; Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'(u(v)); x₀ := Φ(v₀) = z + ιv₀ + ι'(u(v₀)); F := fderiv ℝ Φ v₀; L := range F, with F viewed as a linear map.

Formalization note: unless split further, this is a machine leaf: one theorem appended to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, with no new import or helper. Every lemma cited is in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.

1. Coercivity. For every v ∈ ℝⁿ, linearity of ι and ι' gives Φ(v) − x₀ = ι(v − v₀) + ι'(u(v) − u(v₀)). The two summands are orthogonal by hypothesis, and ι, ι' preserve norms (LinearIsometry.norm_map). By Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero), ‖Φ(v) − x₀‖² = ‖v − v₀‖² + ‖u(v) − u(v₀)‖² ≥ ‖v − v₀‖². As both norms are nonnegative, ‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − x₀‖.

2. Differentiability.
- v ↦ z + ιv is differentiable at v₀: it is a constant plus the continuous linear map ι.
- v ↦ ι'(u(v)) is differentiable at v₀: it is the continuous linear map ι' composed with u, which is differentiable at v₀ by hypothesis.
Hence Φ is differentiable at v₀, and HasFDerivAt Φ F v₀.

3. Little-o estimate.
- By HasFDerivAt.isLittleO, (v ↦ Φ(v) − x₀ − F(v − v₀)) = o(v ↦ v − v₀) as v → v₀.
- For the given ε > 0 (IsLittleO.def): eventually for v near v₀, ‖Φ(v) − x₀ − F(v − v₀)‖ ≤ ε‖v − v₀‖.
- By Metric.eventually_nhds_iff there is ρ > 0 such that this inequality holds for every v with dist(v, v₀) < ρ. This is the required ρ.

4. Let y ∈ Φ(D) with dist(y, x₀) < ρ, and write y = Φ(v) with v ∈ D.
- By step 1, dist(v, v₀) = ‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − x₀‖ = dist(y, x₀) < ρ.
- Put t := F(v − v₀); then t ∈ L (LinearMap.mem_range_self).
- By step 3, and then step 1 with ε ≥ 0: ‖y − x₀ − t‖ = ‖Φ(v) − x₀ − F(v − v₀)‖ ≤ ε‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ε‖y − x₀‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pythagoras with ⟨ιa, ι'b⟩ = 0 and norm preservation gives ‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v₀)‖ for every v.
Φ = z + ι + ι'∘u is differentiable at v₀. The little-o estimate gives ρ > 0 with ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v₀) − DΦ(v₀)(v − v₀)‖ ≤ ε‖v − v₀‖ whenever dist(v, v₀) < ρ.
For y = Φ(v) ∈ Φ(D) with dist(y, Φ(v₀)) < ρ, coercivity gives dist(v, v₀) < ρ. Then t := DΦ(v₀)(v − v₀) ∈ range DΦ(v₀) satisfies ‖y − Φ(v₀) − t‖ ≤ ε‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ε‖y − Φ(v₀)‖.

Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k be differentiable at v₀ ∈ ℝⁿ, let z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, and put Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v). Then the linear subspace range DΦ(v₀) ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} has dimension n. Here DΦ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ Φ v₀, viewed as a linear map.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof of dgcr_approxTangent_eq_graph_tangent. There, DΦ(v₀) = ι + ι'∘Du(v₀) satisfies ι*DΦ(v₀) = id, hence is injective, so L = range DΦ(v₀) is n-dimensional. Here injectivity is shown directly by Pythagoras instead of through the adjoint ι*; this is the same orthogonality computation.

Notation: ℝ^m = Euclid m; Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'(u(v)); Du := fderiv ℝ u v₀.

Formalization note: unless split further, this is a machine leaf: one theorem appended to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, with no new import or helper. Every lemma cited is in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.

1. Derivative.
- The map v ↦ z + ιv has derivative ι at v₀: the continuous linear map ι is its own derivative, and adding a constant does not change it (HasFDerivAt.const_add).
- The map v ↦ ι'(u(v)) has derivative ι' ∘ Du at v₀ by the chain rule, since u is differentiable at v₀ and ι' is a continuous linear map.
By the sum rule (HasFDerivAt.add), HasFDerivAt Φ F v₀ with F := ι + ι' ∘ Du. Hence fderiv ℝ Φ v₀ = F (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), i.e. F h = ιh + ι'(Du h).

2. Injectivity. Suppose F h = 0, i.e. ιh + ι'(Du h) = 0. The two summands are orthogonal by hypothesis. By Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero) and norm preservation of ι and ι', 0 = ‖ιh + ι'(Du h)‖² = ‖h‖² + ‖Du h‖². Hence ‖h‖² = 0 and h = 0. So ker F = ⊥ (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot'), and F, as a linear map, is injective.

3. Dimension. For an injective linear map, the range has the dimension of the domain (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). So finrank (range F) = finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). ∎
proof_key_steps: Sum and chain rules give DΦ(v₀) = ι + ι'∘Du(v₀).
Pythagoras with orthogonality gives ‖DΦ(v₀)h‖² = ‖h‖² + ‖Du(v₀)h‖², so DΦ(v₀)h = 0 forces h = 0; hence DΦ(v₀) is injective.
Rank–nullity for injective maps: finrank range DΦ(v₀) = finrank ℝⁿ = n.
